[LFST.9.2.1] **A replayable event trace.** A trace is replayable when it holds
every recordable event the engine emitted, as [RFCS.3.6] records it: an
inject-class atom for every input the engine consumed, a compare-class atom for
every observable [RFCS.3.6] gives an atom, and every clock value it observed
([RFCS.17.1]). Its prelude also carries the host's cache seeds, which are
starting state and no event ([RFCS.26.1]). An event of a kind [RFCS.3.6] gives no atom is not in a trace,
and its absence does not make the trace unreplayable. A replayable trace is replayed
against an engine configured as the recording one was: the trace carries no
engine setting, and configuration is a precondition of replay ([LDET.2.7]).

**The engine must emit all three, so producing a replayable trace is not a
discipline the integrator follows** ([LFST.1.3]). An integrator that subscribes
to the whole surface and records what it receives holds one by construction. A
trace is unreplayable only where a subscriber filtered, and a replayer **must**
refuse such a trace rather than report the absent events as divergences.

**Replay drives the engine from the trace's own clock.** The replayer applies
each `ClockAdvance` before the atoms that follow it ([RFCS.10.5]), so every
re-derived atom's `clock_ns` reproduces. Where the recording engine read that
clock from is immaterial — a wall-clock reading written into a `ClockAdvance`
is a recorded number like any other. What matters is that the engine recorded
**every** value it observed, which [RFCS.10.3] requires of it.

**Cadence is likewise the recorder's obligation and not the replayer's
problem.** The replayer fires the engine to quiescence ([RARC.5.6.6]) between
the inputs the trace marks as separately pumped, and the trace marks them
because the engine emits a pump boundary rather than leaving a reader to infer
one.

**One fault ends a trace rather than making it unreplayable.** A
`pump_wcet_ns` overrun halts the tier ([RTCT.7.3]), so the `EngineError` it
emits is the last record on the trace. A replayer drives the trace to that
point, comparing every atom before it, and stops there; the terminal fault is
the recorded run's cause of death, not an observable the replay must reproduce.
That is the only cap of [RTCT.7.1] decided on a measurement rather than on a
count the engine holds, and it is the only place a replay meets a recorded atom
it does not compare.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_net
idris.note: The canonical cadence: one input, then a pump.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_net
idris.note: A history: the inputs, each pumped, in order.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__agree_after_history
idris.note: THE TRANSFER OF CONTENT, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network, every terminal holds exactly the unblocked matches FireLoop's recompute gives the rule its chain lowers to. Order and flags are part two.

idris.name: iret_19_5__run_clocked
idris.note: The clause's cadence folded over a list of inputs: each pumped to quiescence before the next, the state and the counts returned together.

idris.name: iret_19_5__run_clocked_cons
idris.note: The cadence unfolded by one input: pump it, then the rest from the state it left.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__after_clocked
idris.note: The state the clause's cadence leaves after a list of inputs. A fixture.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_clocked
idris.note: The clause's cadence -- one input, then a pump to quiescence -- on the clocked network.

idris.name: iret_7_9_2__acquire_after_history
idris.note: THEOREM 6, closed at the top: after any history every live fact is rejected by every activation's NOT nodes that admit it.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_unique
idris.note: One input pumped keeps one live fact per key.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_unique
idris.note: Every history keeps one live fact per key.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__replay
idris.note: The replay's history under the dense reading: the surviving facts, by assertion.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_net_view
idris.note: One input pumped keeps the view.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_net_view
idris.note: EVERY HISTORY keeps the view.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__prepared_net
idris.note: The inputs of a replay prepared with no pump between them; the clause's cadence pumps after each, which is the special case of one input.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__prepared_clocked
idris.note: The inputs of a replay prepared with no pump between them, ticks re-timing as they go; the clause's cadence pumps after each, which is the special case of one input.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_net_ordered
idris.note: One input pumped keeps the order.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_net_ordered
idris.note: EVERY HISTORY keeps the order.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_g
idris.note: One input pumped, with the set beside it.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_g_fst
idris.note: The ghost's boundary is the model's.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_sound
idris.note: One input pumped keeps the ghost sound.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_g
idris.note: A history with the set beside it.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_g_fst
idris.note: THE GHOST SHADOWS THE ENGINE through every history: its engine component is the engine of Rete/Network.idr.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_sound
idris.note: EVERY HISTORY keeps the ghost sound.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__consumed
idris.note: The inputs of a replay, each at its sample, with no pump between them; the clause's cadence pumps after each, the one-step case.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__consumed_is_prepared
idris.note: A replay's sampled inputs are prepared inputs with the samples made explicit.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__cycles
idris.note: The cadence folded over the ticks: one input then a pump. A fixture.

idris.name: Lfst_9_2_1__canonical_net
idris.note: A canonical replay on the network: each input pumped to quiescence, in order.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_tms_net
idris.note: The canonical cadence on the network: one input, then a pump.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_tms
idris.note: The same history on FireLoopTms's engine, under one fuel.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_tms_net
idris.note: A history on the network with truth maintenance: the inputs, each pumped, in order, under one fuel.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__boundary_tms_agree
idris.note: AN INPUT PUMPED agrees: the input, then the run, with the same halt and count.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__canonical_tms_agree
idris.note: A CANONICAL REPLAY ON FIRELOOP IS CANONICAL ON THE NETWORK, input by input with the same fuel: each pump quiesces on both sides, and the states agree throughout.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__replay_tms_agree
idris.note: EVERY HISTORY keeps the agreement, under one fuel.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer_canonical
idris.note: THE CANONICAL TRANSFER: a canonical replay from FireLoopTms's empty state is a canonical replay from the loaded network, with the same fuel per input, and the states agree at its end.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer_tms
idris.note: THE TRANSFER THEOREM WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE: run on one history from the loaded network and from FireLoopTms's empty state under the program the network lowers to, the two engines reach one working memory and one dependency table, and each table's unblocked tokens are the terminal's activations, in order and with their flags. Every theorem stated over FireLoopTms's run -- Rete/TmsRun.idr, Lcyc/TmsTermination.idr, Rete/PumpBoundary.idr -- is a theorem about the spec's network.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_1__step
idris.note: The canonical cadence is one shape of step sequence; a batched pump -- the clause's live optimisation outside verify-replay -- is another, and the Idris model runs the one the fixture wrote.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__boundary_agree
idris.note: AN INPUT PUMPED agrees: the input, then a run to quiescence or out of fuel, on both sides.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__replay_agree
idris.note: EVERY HISTORY keeps the agreement: the inputs in order, each pumped, on both sides.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer
idris.note: THE TRANSFER THEOREM: run on one history from the loaded network and from FireLoop's empty state under the program the network lowers to, the two engines reach one working memory, and each table's unblocked tokens are its terminal's activations, in order and with their flags. Against the plain pipeline, inputs without Rete/PumpBoundary.idr's TMS phase and without the clock; Rete/NetworkTmsTransfer.idr carries the phase and Rete/NetworkTtl.idr the clock, on this agreement.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_plain
idris.note: The canonical cadence without the TMS phase: one input, then a pump.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_plain_well
idris.note: One input pumped keeps the state well-formed.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_plain
idris.note: A history on FireLoop without the TMS phase: the inputs, each pumped, in order.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_plain_well
idris.note: EVERY HISTORY keeps a FireLoop state well-formed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__well_after_history
idris.note: FIRELOOP'S STATE AFTER ANY HISTORY -- inputs applied without the TMS phase, each pumped -- is well-formed: every table in the key's order.

idris.name: Lfst_9_2_1__canonical_ttl_net
idris.note: A canonical replay with ticks on the network: each input pumped to quiescence.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_ttl_net
idris.note: The canonical cadence with ticks on the network: one input, then a pump.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__boundary_ttl_agree
idris.note: AN INPUT PUMPED agrees: the steps before firing, then the run, same halt and count.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__canonical_ttl_agree
idris.note: A CANONICAL REPLAY WITH TICKS ON FIRELOOP IS ONE ON THE NETWORK, input by input with the same fuel, and the states agree throughout -- one working memory, one dependency table, one deadline table, one clock.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer_ttl
idris.note: THE TRANSFER WITH TICKS: a canonical replay with ticks from FireLoop's empty state is one from the loaded network, and at its end the two agree. Rete/TtlSweep.idr's theorems are theorems of the network.

idris.name: Lfst_9_2_1__canonical
idris.note: A canonical replay: each input pumped to quiescence, in order.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary
idris.note: The canonical cadence: one input, then a pump.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_inv
idris.note: One boundary keeps the run invariant and the target kinds, however the pump halted.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__canonical_exists
idris.note: THE CANONICAL REPLAY EXISTS. For a positive program certified as [LCYC.3.1.1] admits it, from an invariant state every input sequence has a replay in which each pump reaches quiescence, and the invariant holds at its end.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__canonical_from_input
idris.note: FROM THE INPUT: the same from the initial state of any input with unique ids, the domain being the program's literals, the input's values and the asserted values. `partial`: 'certified' is the kind-level certificate, which a program [LCYC.3.1.1] admits only through [LCYC.6.1]'s literal break lacks.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__canonical_inv
idris.note: A canonical replay keeps the invariant to its end, so at every boundary along the way.

idris.name: Lfst_9_2_1__canonical_ttl
idris.note: A canonical replay with ticks: each input pumped to quiescence, in order.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_ttl
idris.note: The canonical cadence with ticks: one input, prepared, then a pump.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_ttl_inv
idris.note: One boundary with ticks keeps the clocked invariant.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__canonical_ttl_exists
idris.note: THE CANONICAL REPLAY WITH TICKS EXISTS: for a certified positive program, from an invariant clocked state every input sequence has a replay in which each pump reaches quiescence.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__canonical_ttl_from_input
idris.note: FROM THE INPUT, with the start clock: the same from any input with unique ids, its TTL facts stamped at the start clock.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__canonical_ttl_inv
idris.note: A canonical replay with ticks keeps it to its end, so at every boundary.
